title: Comparatives & Superlatives I
subtitle: Compare two things, or say which one is the most/least in a group.
objectives: Form comparative adjectives (bigger, more interesting, less expensive)
Form superlative adjectives (the biggest, the most interesting, the least expensive)

content.intro: You use comparisons every day — this house vs. that one, this year vs. last year. English forms them differently depending on how long the adjective is.

rules.heading: a) Comparative — two things
rules.body:
• Short adjectives (1 syllable, or 2 ending in -y): add -er → bigger, taller, happier
  • Long adjectives (2+ syllables): more/less + adjective → more interesting, less expensive
  • Equality: as + adjective + as → as big as
  • Inferiority: less + adjective + than → less expensive than

rules.heading: b) Superlative — three or more things
rules.body:
• Short adjectives: the + adjective + -est → the biggest, the tallest
  • Long adjectives: the most/least + adjective → the most interesting, the least expensive

examples: This house is bigger than that one.
She is as tall as her sister.
This book is more interesting than the other one.
This is the most beautiful place I have ever seen.
My car isn't as fast as yours.
She is the smartest student in the group.

commonMistakes.wrong: This book is more interesting as the other one.
commonMistakes.right: This book is more interesting than the other one.
commonMistakes.why: The comparative uses "than," not "as," to compare two things.

commonMistakes.wrong: She is the more smart student.
commonMistakes.why: "Smart" is a short adjective — use -est, not "more."

commonMistakes.right: This is the most beautiful place.
commonMistakes.why: "Beautiful" is a long adjective — use "the most," not -est.

commonMistakes.wrong: My car is fast as yours.
commonMistakes.right: My car is as fast as yours.
commonMistakes.why: Equality needs "as" on both sides: as + adjective + as.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct comparative or superlative form.

items.prompt: This house is ___ (big) than that one.
This book is ___ (interesting) than the other one.
This is ___ (beautiful) place I have ever seen.
items.explanation: Long adjective, superlative: the most + beautiful.

items.prompt: She is ___ (smart) student in the group.
items.explanation: Short adjective, superlative: smart → the smartest.

items.prompt: Today is ___ (hot) day of the year.
items.explanation: Short adjective ending in a single vowel+consonant doubles the consonant: hot → hottest.
Equality needs "as + adjective + as": is as tall as.

items.prompt: He is ___ than his brother. (less young)

items.incorrect: This task is more difficult as the last one.
answer: This task is more difficult than the last one.

items.incorrect: She is the intelligentest person I know.
answer: She is the most intelligent person I know.
items.explanation: "Intelligent" is a long adjective — use "the most," not -est.

summary: Equality: as + adjective + as. Comparative always pairs with "than," never "as."
